name: bonk-air4-wheel
notes: Concept for air.4 Acrobatic Double Slice, on its existing move-data clock (73 ticks, hitbox 37-48, IASA 63).
character: Bonk (55 joints, five fingers; a 1.84 m greatsword fixed to the right hand as joint Weapon0 with bladeHilt and bladeEnd anchors)
image_notes: 1: the fall entry pose with the greatsword resting on the right shoulder (profile, front, three-quarter rear angle). 2: Bonk's own two-handed grip, from his Charging Double Slash (front, three-quarter, profile).
description:
Acrobatic Double Slice (air.4), Bonk's aerial kill move, as a greatsword wheel: one full forward somersault with the arms and blade stretched overhead, so blade and body turn as one giant wheel.

Bonk is the roster's heaviest fighter and its high-jumping acrobat: a hunched brute with huge arms, short legs and a head set low between the shoulders, swinging a 1.84 m greatsword. His aerials should look heavy and acrobatic at once.

Make the sword look heavy. In the air there is no ground to push from, so the whole body swings the blade: hips and chest wind up first and unwind first; the arms follow and the blade comes last, trailing behind the hands until it whips through. The wind-up is slow and readable, the strike takes a few fast ticks, and after contact the blade's momentum carries on and drags the body after it before Bonk reins it in (overshoot, then settle): never stop the blade dead. The legs balance the swing: they tuck to wind up and swing the opposite way to the blade during the strike.

Beats. Tick 0 is the fall pose: the sword rests on his right shoulder with the blade diagonally across his back. Ticks 1-6: the left hand comes up in front of the chest and takes the grip below the right hand. Ticks 1-16: lean back and raise the sword with both arms stretched above the head, the blade pointing up and a little back, knees up: a tall, arched silhouette. Ticks 17-36: the somersault: he tucks his knees and starts rolling forward around his waist, slowly at first, then faster; the arms stay stretched overhead and the blade trails a little behind the turn. Contact at tick 37: the blade catches up: his body is about horizontal and face down, arms and blade stretched straight ahead in one long line at about hip height, the widest point of the wheel. Ticks 38-48: the roll continues and the blade sweeps down in front of and under him as he turns upside down (head below the hips by about tick 45). Ticks 49-63: he completes the forward turn (360 degrees in total), legs coming over the top; the left hand lets go and the sword goes back onto the right shoulder. Ticks 63-73 equal the entry pose. The blade must not cut through his body or legs.
